Who said “Man is something that shall be overcome”?

The located source for this passage, the original-language wording where one exists, and the forms of it that circulate without the attribution.

The recorded source

Attributed to
Friedrich Nietzsche
Work and locator
Thus Spoke Zarathustra, Prologue
English wording
“Man is something that shall be overcome.”
Original wording (German)
Der Mensch ist etwas, das überwunden werden soll.

“Man is something that shall be overcome.” From Zarathustra's prologue; the verb is sollen, a requirement, not a prediction.

Exact wording and the variants in circulation

A quotation in English from a German source has two versions, and they are not interchangeable.

The wording recorded here is the one this archive holds. These are the forms that circulate in its place:

  • “Man is something that shall be overcome.”
  • “Man is something to be surpassed.”

Attribution notes

Nietzsche, Also sprach Zarathustra, Prologue §3. The speaker is Zarathustra addressing the marketplace crowd about the Übermensch; quoting it as Nietzsche's bare definition of humanity without that frame turns a prophetic demand into a slogan about self-improvement.

Who said “Man is something that shall be overcome.”?

The passage is attributed to Friedrich Nietzsche, in Thus Spoke Zarathustra, Prologue. Nietzsche, Also sprach Zarathustra, Prologue §3. The speaker is Zarathustra addressing the marketplace crowd about the Übermensch; quoting it as Nietzsche's bare definition of humanity without that frame turns a prophetic demand into a slogan about self-improvement.

What is the exact wording of the quotation from Friedrich Nietzsche?

The wording recorded here is: “Man is something that shall be overcome.” The German reads: Der Mensch ist etwas, das überwunden werden soll. “Man is something that shall be overcome.” From Zarathustra's prologue; the verb is sollen, a requirement, not a prediction. Forms in circulation that differ from this wording: Man is something that shall be overcome. / Man is something to be surpassed.
